chunks: And by this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He who has in his heart an iota of pride will not enter Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What level of pride prevents a person from entering Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from the Imams highlights that pride is not merely a social flaw but a spiritual blockage that nullifies faith, a concept deeply explored in Shia tafsir regarding the fall of Iblis. The use of 'mithqal dharrah' (weight of a particle) underscores the severity of even the slightest trace of arrogance, contrasting with the humility exemplified by Imam al-Husayn (AS). It serves as a critical criterion for self-purification (tazkiyah) before the final judgment.
